clue.text: Smashing tennis on part of the Surrey side

indicators.note: smashing breaks the three words tennis, on and part to pieces for rebuilding

explanation.surface: A tennis match on the south London side of the river produces some smashing shots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' looks like praise of the tennis, but it tells you to rearrange TENNIS ON PART. Transpontine literally means across the bridges: to a Londoner, the south bank of the Thames, historically in the county of Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Transpontine means lying across the bridges, which for London is the south bank, once part of Surrey.

clue.text: Bit of mosaic of D'Urberville period

parts.note: Tess of the D'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's novel, so a D'Urberville is Tess
an era is a period of history

explanation.surface: A fragment of mosaic is dated to the era of Hardy's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: TESS is the heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel Tess of the D'Urbervilles.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles or cubes that are set together to form a mosaic.

clue.text: . Polonius fell behind here

parts.note: in Hamlet, Polonius hides behind a tapestry hanging and is stabbed through it by Hamlet

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Hamlet, Polonius eavesdrops from behind a wall hanging and Hamlet runs him through it. 'Fell behind' sounds like lagging, but here he literally falls dead behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a woven tapestry wall hanging, like the one Polonius hid behind when he was killed.

clue.text: Craving drink — easily led

parts.note: to sup is to drink, taking liquid in sips
a pliant person is compliant and easily influenced

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a drink is easily led astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craving' here means begging humbly, not desiring.
explanation.definitionFit: A suppliant is someone begging humbly, so the adjective describes a petitioner pleading for favour.

clue.text: None held in honour, blow it!

indicators.note: held in means the first letter sits inside the word for the honour

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
O, the figure nought, stands for none

explanation.surface: An exasperated person complains that nobody has been given an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire. 'Blow it!' sounds like an exclamation of annoyance but defines an instrument you blow.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument, played by blowing through a double reed.

clue.text: Points in the right direction — it makes a difference

indicators.note: a difference in the order of the words it makes a gives a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Pointing the right way, someone says, really matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It makes a difference' reads as a stock phrase, but 'difference' signals rearranging IT MAKES A.
explanation.definitionFit: To take aim is to line up a weapon or shot so it is directed at the target.

clue.text: A patient helper

parts.note: read 'patient' as a noun, someone in hospital, rather than an adjective meaning forbearing

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to describe a helper who is patient; really it is someone who helps a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse cares for the sick, helping patients in a hospital or at home.

clue.text: Declare, not for the first time, soldiers need a lock-up

definitions.text: Declare, not for the first time

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers in the British Army

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for a lock of hair is read from the bottom

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Insisting again that the troops require a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock-up' looks like a jail, but it splits into a lock of hair and 'up', the reversal signal in a down clue. The Royal Engineers are the British Army's corps of military engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassert is to state a claim again, insisting on it once more.

clue.text: Afternoon service?

parts.note: not a church service held in the afternoon but a set of crockery used for afternoon tea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a church service; here it is a set of dishes, as in a dinner service.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea set is the matching cups, saucers and pot used for serving tea, a typical afternoon ritual.

clue.text: Come to blows at work — may well be given a pasting!

definitions.text: may well be given a pasting!

parts.note: to scrap is to fight, coming to blows
a book is a written work

explanation.surface: People who start fighting at work may well get beaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pasting' sounds like a beating, which fits the fight; but it means having things pasted in.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapbook is an album into which cuttings and pictures are glued.

clue.text: The official setting right Eastern first lady

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: An official puts right the first lady of an eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' looks like a president's wife but is EVE, the first woman in Genesis. A reeve was a local official in medieval England.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval English magistrate or manorial overseer, a local officer of the crown or lord.

clue.text: See about a Spanish agreement without any trouble

indicators.note: about means the city's letters go round the other pieces

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is a cathedral city with its own see
si is Spanish for yes

explanation.surface: Someone reviews a deal made with Spain without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese: ELY, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily means with no difficulty, done effortlessly.

clue.text: Values jennets?

definitions.meaning: to value something is to judge its worth
jennets are female donkeys, so jokingly they are she-asses, as a lioness is a she-lion

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a joke: split as ASS-ESSES, it is a mock plural of 'assess', a female ass, which is what a jennet is.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to estimate worth, and the whimsical second reading makes she-donkeys of the word.

clue.text: Course taken ..by high-minded people

parts.note: high-minded is read literally as people whose minds are up in the sky, so their course is a route through the air

explanation.walkthrough: 'High-minded' normally means principled; read literally, it is people flying high.
explanation.definitionFit: An airway is a regular route followed by aircraft, a path through the sky.

clue.text: Alleviates the situation in cut, back

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other
back means the word for cut is written in reverse

parts.note: to sever is to cut
the lie of the land is its situation or layout

explanation.surface: Something eases the situation caused by spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut-back' looks like economy, but it is SEVER turned back into REVES, with LIE placed in it. 'The lie' is how things lie, the situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve is to ease pain or distress, lessening a burden.

clue.text: Dissipated girl shut up

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
pent means confined, shut up, as in pent-up

explanation.surface: A dissolute young woman is locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissipated' here means wasted, as money is, not debauched.
explanation.definitionFit: Misspent means squandered or wasted, as in a misspent youth.

clue.text: Strong binding

definitions.meaning: strong and well built, as a burly young man
fastening with bands of leather or cloth

explanation.definitionFit: Strapping describes a sturdy, robust person, and is also the material or act of tying things with belts.

clue.text: Meet with a number at the border

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
on can mean at, as in on the coast
a verge is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Encountering someone with a figure at a frontier crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is C, the Roman numeral for 100.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines converge when they come together at a point, so to converge is to come together.

clue.text: Account for connection

definitions.meaning: a narration or telling of events
a link or association between things, or a kinsman

explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a narrated story and also a link between things or people.

clue.text: Note before and after position for standing

indicators.note: before puts the first note ahead of the word for position
and after places a further note behind the word for position

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
to put is to position or place
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A message written before and after taking up a post, about one's standing.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'Note' serves twice: a sol-fa note goes before the word for position, and a lettered note after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Repute is reputation, one's standing in the eyes of others.

clue.text: Gave an address to read out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of to read being thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone delivered a speech by reading it aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read out' seems to describe the speech, but 'out' tells you to rearrange TO READ.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, so gave an address is its past tense.

clue.text: Possibly got in the doctor — up to only a gentle pace

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters sit inside the doctor's abbreviation

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of got may come in another order
in a down clue, up means the little word to is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: Perhaps the doctor was fetched, though he came only at a slow trot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges GOT to OGT, which goes 'in' DR; 'up' reverses TO to OT at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogtrot is an easy, unhurried jogging gait, like that of a trotting dog.

clue.text: Keep petty-cash book

parts.note: P for penny or pence stands for small change
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Hold on to the ledger for petty cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petty-cash book' looks like one accounting item but splits: P (a penny) and 'book' as a verb, RESERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve is to maintain or save something from harm or decay.

clue.text: Leaderless men plead to follow

indicators.note: leaderless means the opening letter of men is dropped

parts.note: to sue is to plead or appeal, as in suing for peace

explanation.surface: Men without a leader beg to follow someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plead' fits the surface sense of begging, but here it is SUE, to plead in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result, so to follow is its sense.

clue.text: Season well

definitions.meaning: one of the four quarters of the year, between winter and summer
a source of water rising from the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Spring is the season after winter and also a natural source of water flowing up from the earth.

clue.text: What one and one make in the East

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: make signals the letters being made into a new word

parts.note: a second I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question about what one plus one adds up to in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One and one make' looks like arithmetic; read as letters, I, AND and I are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a great country of Asia, part of what the West called the East or the Orient.

clue.text: Pip will accompany her until midnight

definitions.text: Pip will accompany her until midnight

parts.words: Pip will accompany her until midnight
parts.note: old British signallers' spelling said P M as two words, so from noon to midnight Pip goes with this woman's name

explanation.walkthrough: In the old British forces' phonetic alphabet, P was 'Pip' and M was the woman's name here, so p.m. (afternoon until midnight) was 'Pip' plus her.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma was the signallers' code word for M, so with Pip it spells p.m., the hours from noon to midnight.

clue.text: Hair used in mattress-making

indicators.note: used in means the word is found inside the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Horsehair is a material used in making mattresses.
explanation.walkthrough: Old mattresses were indeed stuffed with hair, so the surface is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a lock of hair, often a long one.

clue.text: Mnemonic about a residuum

indicators.note: about means the word for a memory aid goes round the a

parts.note: a mnemonic is a memory aid, something that jogs the memory

explanation.surface: A memory aid concerning what is left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mnemonic' tempts as anagram fodder, but its letters do not fit; it is REMINDER, around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A residuum is what is left after the rest is removed, the leftover part.

clue.text: Usual allowance for an American soldier

parts.note: general means usual or widespread, as in the general rule
a grant is a sum allowed, such as a student's allowance

explanation.surface: A standard payment given to a US serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses S. Grant was the Union commander in the American Civil War and later president.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant was a Union commander in the US Civil War, a famous military leader of America.
